question: A nursing student is counseling a new mother who fears that modern contraceptives cause permanent infertility. How should the student respond?

question: A patient is prescribed a metered-dose inhaler without a spacer and complains that the medicine just hits their throat. What is the best nursing action?

question: How does using the nursing process in critical care differ from a normal ward?

explanation: When an infection starts somewhere else (like your lungs or throat), germs can hitch a ride in the bloodstream (hematogenous means 'blood-borne') and end up crossing over into the brain. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T17#GNS222_U3_T17_h1)

question: Up to how many weeks of pregnancy is an abortion generally defined to occur?

options.A: Under 20 to 22 weeks of gestation
options.B: Any time after 40 weeks of gestation
options.C: At exactly 28 weeks of gestation
options.D: Between 32 and 36 weeks of gestation

explanation: We define an abortion as the end of a pregnancy before the baby can survive outside the womb, which is generally under 20 to 22 weeks. You've got this! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T005#GNS226_U5_T005_h1)

question: A patient only opens their eyes and groans when you firmly pinch their shoulder. How do you document this level of consciousness?

options.A: Comatose
options.B: Alert
options.C: Stuporous
options.D: Lethargic

explanation: A stuporous patient is deeply sleepy and only reacts with sounds or movement when given strong or painful stimulation. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T2#GNS222_U3_T2_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT a normal sign of simple pregnancy heartburn?

options.A: Worsening discomfort after eating a large meal
options.B: A sour taste at the back of the throat
options.C: A burning feeling behind the breastbone
options.D: Crushing chest pain radiating to the jaw

explanation: Crushing jaw pain points toward heart trouble, not regular acid reflux. Good clinical spotting! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T013#GNS226_U2_T013_h4)

question: What is the first thing a nurse should do when they notice skin scars during a physical exam?

options.A: Immediately report the client to local police
options.B: Scold the client for undergoing dangerous practices
options.C: Inspect the skin calmly and professionally
options.D: Refuse to touch the affected body part

explanation: Well done! Nurses always maintain a warm, non-judgmental attitude and perform thorough assessments to understand a client's history. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T7#GNS225_U6_T7_h5)

question: What happens if you use a single-dose medication vial for more than one patient?

options.A: It changes the chemical concentration of the prescribed drug
options.B: It transfers invisible pathogens between patients via contaminated equipment
options.C: It causes the remaining medicine to expire instantly
options.D: It increases the physical pain experienced during injection

explanation: Single-dose vials don't have preservatives. Reusing them lets germs multiply and spread infections to the next patient. Always use one vial per patient! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T2#GNS122_U3_T2_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of a clinical guideline in nursing?

options.A: To punish nurses who make minor documentation errors
options.B: To help nurses make evidence-based care decisions
options.C: To increase the cost of hospital equipment purchasing
options.D: To replace doctors completely in the labor room

explanation: Guidelines provide clear, research-backed instructions so nurses know the best steps to take for specific health problems. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T3#GNS312_U5_T3_h2)

question: What does the term 'cachexia' mean in advanced illness?

options.A: A sudden increase in daily appetite
options.B: Complete blockage of the large intestine
options.C: An infection caused by poor dental hygiene
options.D: Severe muscle wasting and weight loss

explanation: You've got this! Cachexia is a whole-body wasting condition caused by disease inflammation, not just because the person isn't eating enough food. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T17#GNS321_U4_T17_h2)

question: What is the main job of Human Chorionic Gonadotropin (hCG) in early pregnancy?

options.A: To signal the corpus luteum to continue producing progesterone
options.B: To lower the mother's blood pressure during the first trimester
options.C: To prepare the fetal lungs for air breathing
options.D: To stimulate milk production in the maternal mammary glands

explanation: Wonderful! hCG is the famous pregnancy hormone that tells the ovary's corpus luteum to keep pumping out progesterone until the placenta is ready to take over. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T008#GNS226_U2_T008_h5)

question: Why do we ask patients to take off all jewelry and metallic objects before an X-ray?

options.A: They make the patient feel too heavy on the table
options.B: They attract stray electrical currents from the machine
options.C: They cause the X-ray tube to overheat quickly
options.D: They create dense white artifacts that hide details

explanation: Metal blocks X-rays completely, leaving bright white spots that might hide important clues on the film. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T10#GNS123_U2_T10_h4)

question: Which nurse behavior is most likely to drive a teenager away from a health clinic permanently?

options.A: Empathetic counseling
options.B: Moralizing and scolding
options.C: Active listening
options.D: Warm greeting

explanation: Teens are super sensitive to criticism. If they expect to be judged or lectured, they'll avoid getting the care they need. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T18#GNS312_U3_T18_h4)

question: What is the main reason for putting a cold compress on a fresh insect sting?

options.A: It kills any bacteria introduced by the insect's mouthparts
options.B: It triggers immediate local histamine destruction
options.C: It completely neutralizes the chemical structure of the acid
options.D: It constricts blood vessels to slow down venom absorption

explanation: Correct! Cold causes the local blood vessels to narrow (vasoconstriction), slowing down how quickly the venom travels into the rest of the body. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T12#GNS221_U3_T12_h4)
